answer: One concrete mechanism: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because umber only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, ripple is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any nebula approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
